references.text: Moses also notes here that Israel's laws demonstrate wisdom and understanding to the nations, underscoring the righteousness and greatness of the law.
The psalmist praises the Lord's law as perfect and righteous, and His commandments as pure and eternal, reflecting the description of Israel's just statutes and laws.
The psalmist affirms that the Lord is righteous and His laws are right, which aligns with the description of just statutes and laws.
The psalm highlights that God declared His word and His laws to Israel, and that He has not done so for any other nation.
Paul notes that the Jews were entrusted with God's words, which include the righteous laws and statutes given to Israel.
Paul lists legislation as one of Israel's special privileges, reflecting Israel's unique position with righteous laws.
Moses refers to the law he imposed on the people as an inheritance for the congregation of Jacob.
The Lord gives statutes and laws by which a person shall live, demonstrating the life-giving and righteous character of the law.
